articles.title: The History of Grand Theft Auto Easter Eggs
articles.summary: We explore the inside jokes and little secrets tucked in every corner of the GTA maps.
articles.body:
When you’ve got an open world as big and dense as Grand Theft Auto, you’ve got to fill it with something. Restaurants, tennis courts, hidden packages, Strangers and Freaks. All kinds of treats to reward our exploration, some buried deeper than others. From hearts and minds to signs and shrines, the inside jokes and little secrets Rockstar’s calling card tucked in every corner of the map. This is the history of Grand Theft Auto easter eggs.

The top-down Grand Theft Autos are too sparse and pixelated for the kind of buried treasures that would await us in the 3D era, but easter eggs exist even in this perspective.

The most famous secret of the first GTA games involves lines of chanting bald NPCs dressed in orange robes, evocative of the Hare Krishna devotees famous for descending upon travelers at airports. If you can run the entire procession down sequentially, you’re rewarded with a seemingly nonsensical shout of “GOURANGA!” The phrase, a Krishna term meaning “be happy,” became the series’ signature meme among the early fanbase and resurfaced in the first few sequels, with hidden bonuses for mowing down Elvis impersonators in GTA 2 and football hooligans in GTA: London.

For a series so devoted to examining the American dream, it’s easy to forget that Grand Theft Auto is British-born. The Scottish studio that created the series and the English brothers who made it a phenomenon belong to a storied Britdev tradition of taking the mick in the margins. From the ZX Spectrum emulator Rare buried in GoldenEye to Team17’s profane cheat codes and salty rants against Amiga Power magazine, British studios excel at hiding cheeky winks within their games. DMA Design, later Rockstar North, is no exception.

DMA logos are disguised among the scenery, the pager randomly rags on staffers, and director Keith Hamilton himself sends you on a mission to find “the elements of GTA.” You can unlock R-rated language by naming your character after the studio’s credited “Project Bloke.” The developers are sharing their private jokes with the players, leaving their signatures in out-of-reach places. It’s been that way since the very first easter egg: The people in the game are talking to us, but they make it hard to hear them.

The developers are very present in GTA 3. The game came in hot, suffered hurried changes, and still showed a lot of its arcadey roots. The veil between the game and its inner workings is thinnest here, you can out of bounds and fly the unflyable dodo across nonexistent towns named after team members. Look to La Luna through the eyes of a sniper rifle and pull the trigger to change the size of the moon, since the devs never decided how big it should be. You had to be willing to break the game a little bit to earn your peek behind the curtain, but it wasn’t that hard to do in 2001.

Rockstar anticipated our escape. If you drive up a staircase near a parking lot in Staunton Island, you can hop out and use your car to climb onto a normally inaccessible roof. A precision jump drops you in an unused back alley, where you’ll find a sign that says “You weren’t supposed to be able to get here, you know.” The devs mercifully included a ramp to get us back into the game proper rather than risking a softlock. They knew we’d be snooping around.

Some developers would dummy out this kind of content once it's discovered, but Rockstar maintained it as a running gag, slapping messages in hard-to-find spots throughout the series. In GTA: Vice City, Tommy can clip through a wall near the VCN helipad to enter a room with a simple marvel pedestal, upon which rests a single egg emblazoned “Happy Easter!”

You’ll find no such ovoid in GTA: San Andreas. The closest you’ll come is the Gant Bridge that connects San Fierro with Las Venturas. The visitor center below contains a display serving up fun facts about the bridge. On closer inspection the text is actually information on the structure’s internal game files, like how it’s made up of 16,000 polygons and takes up a “staggering 1.27mb of disc space.” The sign was actually updated by Grove Street Games for the Definitive Edition release. After 17 years, the bridge’s triangle count doubled, the textures increased fourfold, and the disk space increased a whopping 3,000 percent. Good thing storage has stayed so affordable!

If CJ can tear himself away from the field trip exhibits and land himself on top of the southern suspension tower, he’ll find another secret scolding among the orange steel rivets: “There are no Easter Eggs up here. Go away.” Clearly anticipating you’d be crushed by the disappointment of your futile search, Rockstar eases the pain with a handy parachute to get you back on your feet.

Grand Theft Auto 4 does the bit, too. And cleverly, though nothing mind-blowing for the most part. A museum placard giving out about how hard the dinosaur skeletons were to sculpt, or a warning inside of the Statue of Happiness, through a door in the base reached only by air. “No hidden content,” reads an engraving by a collision-free closed door. Walk through the illusory wall, however and you’ll encounter something far more visceral than anything that’s come before.

Inside you’ll find a ladder vanishing upwards into the body of the rusted copper colossus. Reach the top and you’ll find a scaffold standing just below a huge and hideous heart. Suspended painfully from chains, its maddening beat thunders inside the internal steel chamber and it cannot die. You’re not going to fit this thing in a bunny’s basket.

It’s a darker, more unsettling easter egg than any that’s come before, even if it’s apparently just a jab at Hillary Clinton, who had gone after Rockstar hard as a senator during the San Andreas Hot Coffee scandal. The Heart of Liberty City is the stuff that creepypastas are made of, legends spread in schoolyards and over IRC. The series had outgrown this style of secret by the time of GTA 5. The mysterious content within its sprawling map goes far beyond the scope of easter eggs, with a nearly cultish following all its own devoted to hunting phantom jetpacks.

Simple secrets like these can be more satisfying than the grand ones. There are no forum flamewars, no rumors to chase for decades, the eggs simply exist to be found in a satisfying fashion. The kind of clean resolution that’s usually reserved for the movies.

There are generally two kinds of easter eggs. We’ve already covered the first, the ones aimed inward where developers poke fun at themselves and the players. Rockstar’s other specialty points outward: hidden homages to media outside their own domain.

In GTA, this overwhelmingly manifests as movie and TV references, but for a few years the developers also took aim at some of their fellow video games, and they were surprisingly nasty about it. There’s a sense of decorum within the game industry, you might poke fun at your rivals but never call them out by name. But Rockstar, never one to follow the rules, seemed personally offended by the existence of competition.

And there was a lot of competition during the golden age of open world 3D action games. An entire cottage industry of “GTA-likes” emerged in the wake of the series’ success, though the biggest target of Rockstar’s ire actually launched years before GTA 3.

1999’s Driver: You Are the Wheelman, from the (you-guessed-it) British developer Reflections Interactive, sees your undercover cop protagonist engage in thrilling high-speed chases throughout realistic cities. While pedestrians are MIA and you can’t commit any crimes, hero John Tanner is able to walk out of his car in the following year’s sequel for some urban exploration, albeit with some highly unusual animation. Driver was well-liked by gamers and critics, but the release of GTA 3 in 2001 more or less made the series obsolete.

Rockstar knew it, too. A mission called “Two-Faced Tanner” features an undercover cop posing as a driver for Yakuza leader Asuka. She tasks our silent hero with taking out the titular Tanner, who, unlike most mission targets, is represented by a unique character model wearing a very familiar suit. If that wasn’t clear enough, one look at this Tanner’s ridiculous run cycle confirms the devs’ malicious intent.

Reflections fired back in their ill-fated Driv-three-er, slipping in a character known as Timmy Vermicelli. Like Vice City’s Tommy Vercetti, Timmy is rocking jeans and a Hawaiian shirt, along with a pair of inflatable water wings to poke fun at the fact that Rockstar’s heroes couldn’t swim.

By this point GTA was already a massive phenomenon, and some petulant mockery from the genre’s first-mover didn’t make much of an impact, especially given Driv3r’s poor reception, but it didn’t fall on deaf ears either. Rockstar was listening, and used GTA: San Andreas to get the final word in the feud.

In the mission “Madd Dogg’s Rhymes,” CJ sneaks past a character playing a video game, who can be heard to remark: “how could Refractions mess up so bad? Tanner, you suck ass!” Harsh? Yes. Petulant? Absolutely. But what do you expect from a company that made a triple-A game about grade school bullies? Rockstar mocked other also-rans like “True Crime: Streets of LA,” insinuating the game was “rubbish” in response to its rather lame parody of Rockstar as “Jock-straps.”

San Andreas was the end of directly attacking the competition. Such petty rivalries were beneath Rockstar now, old grudges buried in the past along with any other game that could possibly compete with them. You can find the memorial in San Fierro graveyard, on a stone reading “RIP Opposition 1997 – 2004.”

It’s hard to believe, but modern Rockstar is actually somewhat classier now, more dignified as befits their goliath stature. You won’t see them getting in the dirt to dish on other games anymore, but film and television are a very different story.

Grand Theft Auto is beholden to cinema. The series is at least 80% made of movies, which is roughly 10% more than famous cinephile Hideo Kojima, and the inspiration is anything but subtle. Entire sequences are lifted from classic films like Heat and Terminator 2. San Andreas simply wouldn’t exist without early ‘90s hood classics like Boyz n’ the Hood, and Vice City is arguably a better Scarface adaptation than the licensed title with Al Pacino’s likeness.

Not every homage is as obvious as Tommy Vercetti gunning down invaders atop his stately manor staircase. Rockstar judiciously scatters movie references throughout their worlds, from NPC chatter to prop design. The most famous of these can be found in Vice City, where a stroll through a random Ocean Beach apartment building reveals a grisly scene within Apartment 3C. Inside, you’ll discover a bloodsoaked bathroom with a chainsaw floating impossibly among the gore, recreating one of the more visceral setpieces from Brian De Palma’s cocaine classic.

You’ll stumble upon lots of these detours and vignettes throughout the games, particularly in Grand Theft Auto 5. Drive far enough into the Chiliad wilderness, perhaps in search of Sasquatches, and you might instead happen upon the aftermath of a drug deal gone wrong, with corpses scattered about a briefcase filled with cash and a dying man warning you not to take it. If you haven’t seen No Country for Old Men, you’ll probably ignore this advice and pocket the dough for a cool $25,000. Even if you have seen it, Trevor Philips and a grenade launcher can probably fend off the assassins who come after you better than Josh Brolin and a bundle of tent poles.

Another secret occurs every night between 7:00 and 8:00 PM, atop a massive cliff in the Chiliad Mountain State Wilderness. Approach the scene by helicopter or watch from a distant road and you’ll see a standoff between law enforcement as two women inside a unique old Tornado, with guitars and a cowboy hat in the backseat that presumably once belonged to Brad Pitt. Rather than surrender, the cornered felons end on their own terms by driving off the cliff, echoing the iconic ending of Thelma and Louise in a parody that’s almost as good as the one in Wayne’s World 2. Unlike the movie, however, we see what happens when the car lands, and it’s not exactly romantic.

There’s much to discover in GTA 5. A ghostly woman who haunts Mount Gordo and writes her killer’s name in blood beneath her. Peyote hallucinations, cryptids and cults. A crashed UFO beneath the sea and the locked hatch from Lost embedded in the Ocean floor, eternally knocking a tap code that translates to “let’s go bowling!”

It approaches a point where the line between “easter egg” and normal content becomes blurry. These indulgences off the beaten path feel different from the winks and nods of yore. They feel more artistic and intentional, without the sense that the developers are surreptitiously speaking to the player.

GTA 6’s Vice City no doubt contains a wealth of secrets among its neon streets to sate our curiosity, but the series might just be too big for easter eggs at this point. It’s no longer made by a handful of irreverent Scots but a team of thousands across the globe. New assets go through untold layers of approvals and quality checks before we’re allowed to see them, and the endless demand for online content means that new murals and mysteries can be introduced at intervals, diluting the magic of old school egg hunts now that the games have grown up.

Charlie "Moose" Lopresto graduated law school, passed the bar, and made a financially questionable decision to write about games and movies instead. Contributing to IGN since 2021, he collects solo board games and transforming robots.

articles.title: 'This Is Akin to a Moon Landing': How Gaming's Top Content Creators Are Preparing for GTA 6's Launch and Beyond
articles.summary: GTA 6 is finally almost here, and the world's biggest content creators are trying to figure out how to handle this behemoth.
articles.body:
GTA 6 is finally upon us and it’s expected to be a cultural juggernaut that overshadows everything in its path. This includes other game releases, movies, and even upcoming holidays, such as Thanksgiving in the United States. Economists estimate a $1 billion loss in productivity during the game’s launch weekend , as millions of people are expected to take time off work to play Rockstar’s highly anticipated game. All in all, it's hard to overstate the impact its arrival will have.

“To me, every GTA feels like a generational moon landing,” said Mary Kish, the Head of Community Marketing at Twitch. “It's so big, and it's so prolific, and it changes culture and my life to such a large extent that it can feel overwhelming.”

However, there is one group of people that are going to be working non-stop for the next month: content creators. Typically, content creators are given games earlier so they can make all kinds of videos about the game. I spoke with some of the top YouTubers and streamers in the world, including in the GTA space, and none of them have the game. That even goes for a popular GTA YouTuber known as TGG, who has 2.32 million subscribers. He was exclusively invited to Rockstar North over the summer to be one of the only people to see GTA 6 before its release and became a primary source for anyone seeking information about the elusive game. And yet, Rockstar withheld the full game even from him.

This isn’t common for a major AAA video game. It shows the lengths Rockstar is going to to preserve and protect its blockbuster, which has been guarded with a veil of secrecy for most of the last decade. Rockstar has been very calculated with how and when it chooses to show what it has been working on. The company has subtly sprinkled short gameplay clips and teasers in the final days before release , but that’s about it. There aren’t any YouTubers who have weeks of uploads banked and ready to go, meaning almost everyone is going into this game completely blind and on the same level playing field.

That has presented a unique situation for a lot of these creators. Everyone I spoke with made it clear that this is a game they are genuinely excited for. Although they have a job to do, they have all waited years for this moment as a fan. Despite the pressure to make content, they all told me they plan to take their time with the game so they can savor it, with some of them estimating that it may take over 100 hours before they actually roll credits on it.

A lot of preparation is going into this launch weekend. Some creators are hiring extra help in the form of additional writers and editors, while others are planning on making a spectacle out of things. Numerous streamers have rented properties in Miami to not only do massive, extravagant streams, but also celebrate the launch with others in person.

Audio tech company JBL, for instance, is sponsoring an event in Miami where streamers like Cody 'Clix' Conrod will be playing the game together in a fancy mansion that they've booked for launch week and will be doing a meet-and-greet at a Micro Center in the city. JBL is using the game's launch as an opportunity to advertise its new JBL Quantum 950X headset.

“I'm especially excited to bring some of my favorite creators together in Miami for a full day of gaming, where we'll be jumping into GTA 6 for the first time, streaming, capturing content and sharing our reactions," said Conrod. "It's going to be an incredible way to experience the game with the JBL community and beyond.”

“GTA 6 represents a landmark moment for gaming culture, bringing together creators and friends of the brand around one of the most highly anticipated releases in entertainment," said Bryce Showalter, JBL's Head of Gaming. "At JBL, we're always looking for ways to show up for the gaming community beyond the headset, creating experiences that connect our technology with the people and cultural moments shaping the industry.

"Our longstanding partnership with Clix is a great example of that commitment, and we’re excited to bring that relationship to life in Miami through opportunities for fans to connect with Clix firsthand at Micro Center, alongside exclusive creator experiences and day-of-release content. JBL is showcasing how Quantum is helping power cultural moments and deliver the immersive audio and all-day comfort players need to stay locked into the game.”

Introducing the Midnight Launch, in celebration of the release of GTA VI Exclusive prizes, game giveaways, merch, and more In Miami, November 18th-19th. Presented by HyperX — Jake Lucky (@JakeSucky) November 11, 2026

Introducing the Midnight Launch, in celebration of the release of GTA VI Exclusive prizes, game giveaways, merch, and more In Miami, November 18th-19th. Presented by HyperX

Gaming peripheral company HyperX is teaming up with Gaming World Media to host a flashy in-person midnight launch event in Miami with fans and streamers. This is not something being done in partnership with Rockstar. It’s just a group of creators and a gaming hardware company putting their money together to do something special. According to GWM co-founder Jake Lucky, the goal is to recapture the magic of a shared in-person gaming experience.

“Essentially we are throwing a party for people who are just as excited for GTA as we are,” said GWM co-founder Jake Lucky in a statement to IGN. “[We are giving] attendees not only a chance to play, but also [a chance to] win their own copy, exclusive merch, and even GTA inspired collectibles to remember the event by. I just really think it’s important to bring back the human aspect of game launches that we have lost in modern times”

This is a big moment for Twitch itself, as GTA 5 has remained a titan on the platform for years. Users have watched around 9 billion hours of the game and 1.7 billion of those hours came in 2025. Kish kept wanting to stress that this moment is “akin to a moon landing” and compared it to a seismic entertainment moment like a new Star Wars or Lord of the Rings film. As a result, they need to make fans feel that on Twitch.

GTA 6 Reveal: 15 New Screenshots, Including 1 Exclusive on IGN

“It's our responsibility as Twitch to say, ‘How do we show up and give them the best GTA experience known to man?’” said Kish. “How do we make this feel reactive and interactive, not passive? Because that's not what we do here. And how do we make you feel like you can be a part of the biggest thing on the planet?”

Twitch is putting all of its energy and money into supporting this launch. Despite not having any official partnership with Rockstar Games, the streaming platform has created custom GTA 6-themed badges that will display next to users who are present for streams of the game during November. The idea is to give fans something similar to signify they were there for a major moment in entertainment history. The company is also giving out 10,000 copies of the game’s Ultimate Edition to random users throughout the month.

Twitch began making its plans “well over six months ago,” according to Kish. Once it became clear that GTA 6 wouldn’t be delayed again, the team began trying to make whatever preparations that it could.

“The GTA tsunami is going to hit us like a ton of bricks and we have to mentally and physically prepare everybody,” said Kish. “All hands on deck, every chef in the kitchen.”

However, despite all of the hype, there has been a bit of discourse in the last week or two before launch. Twitch streamers like Ludwig Ahgren have noted that regardless of how great the game is, its moment might be a blip given it's a single-player game at launch. He suggested that this means that the amount of fun someone could have streaming the game may only last a week or two, but also suggested that viewership might drop because fans will want to experience the game themselves.

Many of the people I spoke to pushed back on this, though. They think this is an opportunity for creators to separate themselves and show their creativity.

“I think you're going to see what certain content creators are made of,” said TGG when speaking with IGN. “I still make some content on GTA 5 single player. I know other creators still make daily [or] weekly content on GTA 5 single player [which is] 13 years old, and GTA 6 is going to be a crazy step above that. I think Rockstar is trying to slow people down. I think Rockstar is trying to get people to live in this world instead of rushing through the story. I think the content creators that lean into that will see far more success than the content creators that don't. The content creators that treat this like a game, a single player story game will be the ones that go to the bottom. The content creators that treat this like a world will probably rise to the top.”

“I think for most streamers, it's probably going to be like we're going to marathon the game, play it, and then that's probably it for most of them,” said Forrest Waldron AKA KreekCraft on Twitch and YouTube. “But I feel like there's a lot you can do, and maybe this is my YouTuber brain talking, but you've got Easter eggs, you've got challenges, you've got speed runs. There's a lot you can do, and especially in a game like this, there's a lot of different things, especially I want to do a fat Jason, fat Lucia play through where you don't exercise them at all and you just make them as big [as possible]. How does that affect the game? So there's a lot of content there.”

Of course, a game like this also means there are a lot of people hoping this will be their big break. Twitch is aware that this an opportunity for smaller names to break out. The platform has made it so anyone can earn money starting from their first stream, if that’s their prerogative. Kish says that Twitch is doing whatever it can to help streamers have the opportunity to succeed.

“I think that there will be people who will make a name for themselves, as there always is every time a major game releases,” said Kish. “I think about times in our history where a game has risen to stardom and then streamers have ridden those coattails not just because the game is good but because that streamer is freaking good and that game propelled them into stardom.

“GTA is going to be a golden ticket for [many] content creators. This is going to propel hundreds if not thousands of content creators to stardom that you have not heard before. There will be names that we will be talking about at Christmas that we do not know today because of GTA. It's going to shake out and we're going to be like panning for creator gold over the next 30 days.”

New creators aren’t the only people trying to achieve something with GTA 6 either. A bunch of extremely popular and established creators who focus on other games and niches are attempting to pivot to GTA with this release. KreekCraft is a Roblox creator with over 17 million subscribers. Up until this summer, he hadn’t really made any content around GTA. He had played the online modes in 4 and 5, but didn’t delve too deep into the story modes. Ultimately, he’s ready to shake things up beyond Roblox and is eager to take a crack at GTA 6.

“As a content creator, I want to do more than just Roblox,” said KreekCraft. “I want to expand out of that. And this is a good opportunity to do that. [...] Part of me is like, I'm so tired of Roblox. I love everybody there, but geez, the decisions they make, it feels like 2012 Activision Blizzard all over again. I don't want to go through this again.

“And then the games, I'm 29 and we're still getting an egg where you run forward and run back, run forward. And it's like, guys, I just can't stream this anymore. And thankfully I'm in a position where I don't have to anymore. And it's like, this is the year I'm going to start prioritizing my mental health and it comes in the shape of this.

The same goes for YouTuber Tyler Smith, AKA tdawgsmitty, who almost exclusively focuses on Call of Duty. However, he has grown tired of the franchise’s annualized antics and has decided that GTA 6 may be an opportunity to find something that makes him a bit happier.

In Pictures: How GTA 6's Jason and Lucia Have Evolved Since 2023

“Today, I sat down and brainstormed for four hours for [GTA 6 video] ideas, and it's like, whoa, I haven't done this in two, three years now because Call of Duty people just want the same thing over and over again,” said Smith.

It’s easy to be cynical and say these guys are just jumping on a bandwagon, but they have legitimate visions for GTA 6 that stretch beyond the first week of hype. It does seem like this is a game where they can break free of tired cycles and flex their creative muscles more. YouTuber Trevor Martin, best known as TmarTn, knows this well.

He also got his start as a Call of Duty YouTuber, with his main channel being dedicated to the shooter franchise. That channel has 3.2 million subscribers… but he hasn’t touched it in seven years. His last video over there was a review of 2019’s Modern Warfare, and then… nothing since then.

Even More GTA 6 Screenshots from Rockstar Games

He pivoted to his second channel that had been mostly let’s play oriented for the better part of a decade. Although he still plays other games, Martin has also become a respected source for aggregating GTA 6 news in the last few years. He estimates that he’s uploaded between 800 - 900 GTA 5 videos, which have accumulated over 200 million views collectively. The decision to move away from Call of Duty wasn’t an intentional one, though.

“Honestly, it wasn't like a decision that I made,” said Martin. “When I uploaded that video, I had no idea I wouldn't upload to that channel again. I think I was really lucky in that sense that it was just super natural and it was just wherever my interests were taking me. Luckily, I had built an audience that loved the let's plays and the walkthroughs and things on the other channels. When COD stopped being fun, I just switched my focus.”

He noted that GTA 6 is a great opportunity for people to break out, whether they be new creators or established ones looking for a new direction. He noted this moment is similar to Fortnite’s release, in that it unexpectedly changed the content creation scene, but this time… everyone is expecting it.

“Obviously everyone knows [GTA 6 is releasing], so everyone's going to be grinding. But if you can stand out, I think it's a huge way to break into the space. I also think it's a great way for established creators to reinvent themselves. There's going to be so much, but at the same time, there's so much in the game to make content on that I feel like you can break the mold and you can do unique things and all it takes is one good idea and you can kind of run with it.”

With everyone wanting to get a slice of the GTA pie, there has been a noticeable uptick in AI-generated videos about the game in the run up to release. There are entire creators who believe this game is their golden ticket, but some of them are going to be letting AI do all of the work for them. Some of these videos have generated hundreds of thousands or even millions of views, despite not being made by humans. TGG was quick to note that a lot of these AI channels blatantly copy his and other creators’ videos.

Martin called it “scary” after seeing how easy it was for someone to easily generate a lengthy video with high-quality assets that he would’ve previously needed a budget and a team to produce.

GTA 6 Vintage Vice City Pack Screenshots

“Those videos, they're pretty well done and they're everywhere and the speed that people can get those out,” he said. “When I watch it, I'm put off by it, but I don't know if other people, especially younger people, are. Because they look great. If you had effects like that back in the day, I remember I used to have effects on [some of my Call of Duty videos], but I had to pay a lot of money for somebody to custom make all these things in [Adobe] After Effects and really highly produce the video. And now it's just a short script away and you can have assets like that.

On one hand, I think it's kind of cool and the technology is amazing. On the other hand, I feel like it kind of loses the love a little bit. You know what I mean? It dehumanizes it. So as tempting as it is, I'm staying super far away from that. I'll stick with simple text PNGs. I don't think videos need that. I think they look nice, but I don't know. I'm really torn on it because I think it's cool, but it's also really concerning.”

Martin went on to note that these types of AI-generated videos excel in informational content. They can rip guides, articles, or summaries from across the internet and spit them out into a new video. As a result, he expects these channels to thrive in the short term with content that teaches players how to make money quickly or unlock certain items. But when it comes to long term success and players looking for more entertaining and original videos? Martin thinks they will “struggle” due the dehumanized nature of AI content.

TGG echoed these sentiments too, noting that a lot of these AI channels blatantly copy their videos.

“I would like to be optimistic and say that people will be able to tell who's being authentic and who's really had these experiences in game and is going along that journey with everyone else,” he said. “And I'd like to think they'd be able to tell the difference between those people and the people that are just riding the hype. I might be wrong. I probably am, but I kind of have to be hopeful that that's the case.”

With GTA 6 being a single-player game at launch, everyone is acutely aware this is only the start of this game’s journey. Although Rockstar itself hasn’t officially announced it, everyone assumes there will be an online mode released later, likely in 2027. After all, GTA Online was a cash cow and Rockstar appears to have laid a fruitful foundation for at least another decade of opportunities and experiences.

The core online experience may only be a sliver of what’s to come for GTA 6. One of the biggest things to spawn from GTA 5 wasn’t actually created by Rockstar itself. Modders created an extremely popular roleplay community that gained a ton of attention during the early 2020s, leading to world renowned figures like LeBron James, Travis Scott, and Kevin Durant all playing the game. Rockstar ended up acquiring the team behind FiveM, which created the modding tools that birthed this content.

Fans expect that Rockstar will utilize this team to build out an official GTA 6 roleplay community across PC and consoles, if not an entire modding system that can be used across platforms. Bethesda has been doing this for about a decade now, but Rockstar may have the resources to push this forward in all kinds of new ways.

“I think the future for Rockstar is going to be definitely in the [user generated content] direction,” said TGG. “I think roleplay has been a crazy explosion, and I don't think anyone quite expected how many people just wanted to live in these worlds that Rockstar is creating, literally live in them. But you're at a point now where you've got three different games in one. You've got GTA single player, you've got GTA Online, and then you have GTA roleplay. And I think the future of content creation has to involve all three.”

With all of that said, it’s clear that GTA 6 is not just a highly-anticipated release for 2026. It’s a game that will set the tone for potentially a whole decade or more when it comes to content creation. New internet personalities are bound to be created, new trends will be set, and as TGG said, it’s a whole new world that is meant to be explored and dug into. It’s the start of a new era and one that we can only begin to imagine the possibilities of.

Cade Onder is a freelancer for IGN's news team. He covers all things entertainment, including gaming, film, and more. You can find him on Twitter @Cade_Onder.

articles.title: NBA 2K27 Is Adding Vice City, GTA 6-Themed Cosmetics, and Much More as Part of Massive Rockstar Games Collaboration
articles.summary: Vice City is coming to NBA 2K27 as part of a massive crossover with GTA 6.
articles.body:
Vice City is coming to NBA 2K27 as part of a massive crossover with GTA 6 .

NBA 2K27's Season 3 update will arrive on November 27, and it's completely focused on GTA 6. The new update will take players to Vice City via a new park next to the city's park. The area features oddles of GTA imagery, including the Vice City blimp that has been flying around Miami in real life and a statue of Macca the Gator, a cartoon character in GTA 6 . Additionally, the season's rewards pass will also give you access to a wide variety of GTA-themed cosmetics and items, including new takeover abilities inspired by the game.

As one might imagine, fans will also be able to rep the new Miami Heat jerseys that were created in collaboration with Rockstar Games. On November 18, the Miami Heat will play a real, regular-season NBA game as the Vice City Heat , complete with new jerseys and a never-before-seen court. It should be quite the spectacle, and one that you will be able to at least partially recreate in-game.

Season 3 will last for seven weeks, and players can actually get in on the action without buying NBA 2K27. If you subscribe to Rockstar's subscription service, GTA+, you will be able to play NBA 2K27 for free from November 27 to January 15. Anyone who pre-orders GTA 6 on Xbox and PlayStation is entitled to a free one-month trial of GTA+, so this would be a great way to put it to use. Starting December 17, subscribers will also be able to take advantage of free GTA-themed items and bonuses in NBA 2K27. Ultimately, it seems like NBA 2K27 doesn't have to worry about fans deleting their games in the same way Madden does .

This update was teased earlier this fall when NBA 2K27 was released , but 2K and Rockstar Games kept a tight lid on what would actually be featured in the update. It appears that this is one of the final marketing beats for GTA 6, as the game will officially release this week. (I know, it's as crazy for me to write as it is for you to read.) The game will have a regional rollout, meaning that folks in New Zealand will technically start playing it a day before users in the United States (unless you take advantage of some loopholes).

GTA 6 is available to pre-load right now , and Rockstar has already pushed out a couple of updates , which fans will need to download before they play the game.

articles.title: The GTA Leaker Who Revealed Lucia — After Hacking Rockstar Through His Hotel TV — Pleads Guilty
articles.summary: Arion Kurtaj, 21, pleads guilty to cybercrimes related to the 2022 Rockstar hack and GTA 6 leaks.
articles.body:
Arion Kurtaj, the Grand Theft Auto 6 leaker who first revealed Lucia to the world, has pleaded guilty to cybercrimes in relation to his 2022 hack of Rockstar . He also pleaded guilty to attempting to extort Rockstar, and to attacking workers at a facility where he was being detained after the hack.

Kurtaj, who is now 21, was 17 when he was initially taken into custody over the 2022 Rockstar hack. As he is from the U.K., he could not initially be named as a minor. He was also deemed unable to stand trial due to the severity of his autism, and was instead sent to be held indefinitely in a secure psychiatric facility . Now, as reported by the BBC , he has been deemed able to stand trial and has entered a guilty plea.

The 2022 hack resulted in the first major GTA 6 leak, as early gameplay footage was shared online. Here, we saw Jason and Lucia for the first time, as they held victims at gunpoint. These clips were shared under the online name TeaPotUberHacker. Rockstar refused to pay Kurtaj's ransom.

Crucially, this was our first confirmation that GTA 6 would star a female protagonist, a first in modern GTA games.

It would be over a year before Rockstar finally confirmed this itself, and even longer until we got an official gameplay reveal, which was only shared in August of this year.

It wasn't just the leaked material that brought attention to this hack in 2022, but also the method in which Kurtaj pulled it off. At the time, police were housing him in a hotel after he was apprehended for previous hacks, fearing he would be targeted by rival hackers. Using his hotel TV, an Amazon Fire Stick, and a Bluetooth mouse and keyboard, Kurtaj was able to breach Rockstar, taking gameplay clips and files.

Rockstar claims that the hack cost them $5 million to recover from. It further claimed that the Lucia reveal was being kept underwraps for the marketing campaign, something that Kurtaj's leaks spoiled.

However, it isn't just these crimes related to the hack that Kurtaj was facing. The BBC also notes that the 21 year old pleaded guilty to physical assaults, in relation to biting workers at the facility where he was being kept.

Kurtaj is awaiting his sentencing. It is unclear if his time at the secure facility will be taken into account should he recieve a custodial sentence.

articles.title: World of Warcraft Raids Are About to Get Easier
articles.summary: As the second season of World of Warcraft Midnight winds down, it's clear that The Venomous Abyss was a bit harder than it should have been.
articles.body:
As the second season of World of Warcraft Midnight winds down, it's clear that The Venomous Abyss was a bit harder than it should have been. And Blizzard is taking the opportunity to make its next raids easier.

Writing via Blizzard's WoW Forum entitled 'raid encounter design in Season 3', World of Warcraft developer Limestone discussed the direction for the final Midnight season, including some of the nerfs coming to The Venomous Abyss nearly three months after launch. The focus here is on "reducing the number of damage events that could kill you or your entire raid with a single individual mistake."

In Midnight's latest raid, The Venomous Abyss, there were a number of abilities, even on Heroic – WoW's middle-tier difficulty – that would wipe your group if you messed up. On the last boss, Ula'Tek, for instance, there were these little snakes that would hatch out of eggs in phase two. They had an ability, called Anguished Cry, that would deal half a million damage to each player within 60 yards and stun them for 6 seconds. That is less than a geared player's health pool, but the stun meant that if a single instance of that ability went off, it would just chain and spiral out of control, leading to the death of you and all of your friends. And that's just one example out of the eight-boss raid.

World of Warcraft: Midnight Cinematic Images and First Screenshots

At least it seems like Blizzard is aware of the problem. In the post, Limestone says it went too far in designing punishing encounters.

"We feel that our design has shifted over time at the expense of the average Mythic player’s experience," Limestone wrote. "Going forward into Season 3, we’d like to intentionally pull back on some of these severe mechanical penalties, even at the start of the season."

The alternative that Blizzard is pitching is that each mistake will be less punishing, but can still spiral out of control. As Limestone stated, "for example, a small missile landing on a character should generally not kill an appropriately geared character from 100% HP. However, if every player in the raid collectively ignores Malacrass’ cast of Eternal Nightfall, he will eventually complete his cast and destroy the raid."

The goal, instead, is to make the successes and failures of raiding a little less binary. Rather than one player messing up a single mechanic and killing 20 people, there will be "fewer wipes that feel like “instant death” and more wipes that feel like a slow unraveling as the group makes mistakes and productively learns from them."

This isn't the first time that Blizzard has had to dial back difficulty in Mythic raiding, and it probably won't be the last. Even back in The War Within , Season 2's Liberation of Undermine raid was a huge step back in difficulty compared to Season 1's Nerub'ar Palace, which Blizzard then corrected with Season 3's Manaforge Omega, which will probably go down in history as one of the best raids of all time. Hopefully Midnight's next raid finds some middle ground once again.

The retail team is probably feeling some added pressure, too, thanks to WoW Forever . I know that I've taken a break from grinding Mythic+ dungeons and raiding in favor of leveling a new Mage on the Classic+ mode, and I know I'm not alone. Hopefully, when the final season of Midnight launches, it feels good enough that it sinks its claws back into me.

Jackie Thomas is the Senior Tech Editor at IGN and the PC components queen. She's been covering gaming hardware for more than a decade for IGN, TechRadar, Gizmodo, PC Gamer and more. You can follow her @Jackiecobra

articles.title: Maika Monroe Won't Return for Longlegs 2, But Is Open to a Future Comeback
articles.summary: Actress and cult horror favorite Maika Monroe has confirmed that she won't return as FBI agent Lee Harker in the upcoming Longlegs sequel, although she's not quite ready to say goodbye to the character for good.
articles.body:
Actress and cult horror favorite Maika Monroe has confirmed that she won't return as FBI agent Lee Harker in the upcoming Longlegs sequel, although she's not quite ready to say goodbye to the character for good.

Speaking to ScreenRant while promoting her latest horror movie, Victorian Psycho, Monroe was asked whether she'd be reprising her role in the follow-up to Oz Perkins' 2024 nerve-shredding nightmare.

"Lee Harker will not be in this one," Monroe confirmed, although her response wasn't entirely straightforward. The actress briefly trailed off with an intriguing "I'll just..." before reiterating that Harker wouldn't appear in the sequel.

However, Monroe added that she "would love to revisit that role," suggesting that while Harker won't be appearing in Longlegs 2, the door isn't necessarily closed on her returning further down the line. It's an interesting development, particularly given how the original movie ended.

Warning: Spoilers for Longlegs follow...

Harker survived her encounter with Nicolas Cage's deeply disturbing serial killer, but her story was hardly wrapped up neatly. After discovering the truth about her mother's involvement in Longlegs' Satanic murders, Harker was left facing the possibility that the evil she'd spent the movie investigating wasn't quite finished with her.

Of course, the bigger mystery surrounding Longlegs 2 is how Nicolas Cage is returning at all, considering his character rather definitively smashed his own face to pieces in the original movie.

Cage is confirmed to reprise his role, with Perkins returning to write and direct. However, plot details remain firmly under wraps, leaving open the possibility that the sequel could actually be a prequel exploring the killer's origins. Given Monroe's apparent absence, that theory is looking increasingly plausible, although nothing has been confirmed.

The sequel is reportedly operating under the working title Hexagram, with production expected to begin in Vancouver in January. Paramount has already scheduled the movie for release on January 14, 2028.

The original Longlegs was a considerable success for Perkins, becoming the highest-grossing movie of his career and establishing Cage's nightmarish serial killer as one of the more memorable horror villains of recent years.

Meanwhile, Monroe has another horror sequel on the way. She's reprising her role as Jay in They Follow, the long-awaited follow-up to 2014's It Follows, which wrapped filming in September.

Whether Lee Harker eventually gets another opportunity to confront the horrors of Longlegs remains to be seen. But given everything the poor woman went through the first time around, perhaps sitting this one out isn't such a bad idea.

Rachel Weber is the Head of Editorial Development at IGN and an elder millennial. She's been a professional nerd since 2006 when she got her start on Official PlayStation Magazine in the UK, and has since worked for GamesIndustry.Biz, Rolling Stone and GamesRadar. She loves horror, horror movies, horror games, Red Dead Redemption 2, and her Love and Deepspace boyfriends.

articles.summary: “Misplaced Parcels” is a Friendship Quest with Hangyodon that hints that there’s a new line of furniture somewhere around Friendship
articles.body:
“Misplaced Parcels” is a Friendship Quest with Hangyodon that hints that there’s a new line of furniture somewhere around Friendship Island in Hello Kitty Island Adventure . But first, you’ll need to help Hangyodon find out what’s happened to his missing order.

To start the quest, talk to Hangyodon at the Comedy Club . It seems that he has a few parcels missing that are meant to contain his new furniture. Help him find out where they went by going with him to My Melody’s shop, Small Gift Big Smile in Seaside Resort .

Hangyodon asks if My Melody has seen any of his furniture that is meant to be shaped like him. My Melody says she hasn’t seen anything come in, but advises that if you were to go to anyone, you should check with Cinnamoroll . He knows where even missing packages go, so it’s only reasonable!

Travel to Spooky Swamp , where Cinnamoroll will be hanging around just outside the Fwishing Well . Losing packages is Cinnamoroll’s biggest nightmare, but he usually feels better after finding them. He takes a quick check in the back (wherever that is), but doesn’t seem to have any trace of Hangyodon’s package. With the trail going cold, you have few options left. Hangyodon suggests going to Retsuko . She’s pretty diligent and has one of those item tracking apps on her phone!

Take the Fast Travel to the Mount Hothead Mailbox , where Retsuko can be found just outside the Ruins Entrance . Retsuko asks for the tracking number, but Hangyodon can’t remember what it was and definitely didn’t write it down. Who does? Well, without that, Retsuko can’t help much.

Talk to Hangyodon again using the [ZL] button since he’s in Companion Mode. You ask if he’s even made the order, and Hangyodon is suddenly a bit doubtful. He can be quite forgetful, and he’s been having a lot of weird dreams lately. Guess you’ll just have to wait to find out what happened and see if Hangyodon makes the order again.

articles.title: Shadow the Hedgehog Gets an 'Unofficial PC Port' — and It Isn’t Vibe Coded
articles.summary: Shadow Recompiled is an unofficial PC port of the 2005 Sonic spinoff, now with achievements and more.
articles.body:
There is no shortage of classic games getting so-called "unofficial PC ports" right now. Previously, these recompilation projects were few and far between because they take a ridiculous amount of time to make. But now, with many modders using generative AI to help them code, they're being pumped out so fast it's hard to keep up.

The problem with this is that not everyone wants to play a game that's vibecoded, either for ethical reasons or due to concerns over the quality. After all, recompiled games are supposed to feel like you are playing a game natively on PC, so expectations are high.

Thankfully, the Sonic community has never shied away from a challenge. Previously, Sonic Unleashed was recompiled and released to play on PC . As long as you could provide your own game files (i.e., prove that you owned the game legitimately on console), you could start playing on PC, with modern-day quality-of-life improvements.

Now, another Sonic game has gotten the same treatment. Or, rather, a Shadow game. Yes, I am of course talking about 2005's Shadow the Hedgehog, originally released for the GameCube, PlayStation 2, and original Xbox.

Released as Shadow Recompiled, this project brings Shadow the Hedgehog to PC, and with modern comforts.

Shadow the Hedgehog (2005) RECOMPILED! Native PC port of the Xbox version (no emulator) Easy installer + PC options menu Widescreen / ultrawide support High / unlocked FPS D3D12 & Vulkan Bloom overhaul + many QoL fixes Achievements Mod support (SA Mod Manager) NO VIBECODE/ AI — TiredAndOnFire-HD Remasters/Gamedev (@TIREDnONFIRE) November 16, 2026

Shadow the Hedgehog (2005) RECOMPILED! Native PC port of the Xbox version (no emulator) Easy installer + PC options menu Widescreen / ultrawide support High / unlocked FPS D3D12 & Vulkan Bloom overhaul + many QoL fixes Achievements Mod support (SA Mod Manager) NO VIBECODE/ AI

Specifically, this brings the Xbox release to PC. But rather than emulating an Xbox, it should run as if it was actually released on PC.

The benefit of these releases is that they can be easier for modders to work with. That means the devs have added a whole new options menu with FPS adjustments, fullscreen toggle, and V-sync, so it should look and run better than ever. There are also achievements and ultrawide monitor support.

As ever, you will have to provide the game files yourself. The devs tell players to do so from a copy of the game they have legally acquired themselves. But once you have that, you can download Shadow Recompiled and get stuck in. Better yet, thanks to mod support, we can expect more fan-made improvements down the line.

Follow Chococat to the Gemstone Beach Mailbox to fast travel to the beaches south of Gemstone Mountain . Once again, there appear to be an odd amount of resources along the beach that don’t normally belong here. Gather them, then return to Chococat so he can log the new coordinates.

With the beach clean, Pekkle drops by and asks what was going on with the beach and the random items that have washed up. Chococat asks Pekkle for his theories on what could be happening with the ocean, to which Pekkle answers with aliens.

Naturally. With this area thoroughly investigated, follow Chococat to Mount Hothead’s beaches.

Pick up: x Swampmallow, 2x Mushrooms, and 1x Pumpkin

Clean up the beach and talk to Chococat once you’re done so he can finish the calculations. Retsuko has joined up with Chococat and shares her thoughts on the alien theory presented by Pekkle before.

articles.title: Is Cam Schlittler the Yankees New Ace?
articles.summary: Gerrit Cole is back. Max Fried is here. But when the Yankees needed one guy to start October, they turned to a 25-year-old from Walpole, Massachusetts. The u...
articles.body:
Gerrit Cole is back. Max Fried is here. But when the Yankees needed one guy to start October, they turned to a 25-year-old from Walpole, Massachusetts. The unexpected rise of Cam Schlittler has captured fans' attention this season.

On Sept. 29, the Yankees faced their rivals, the Boston Red Sox, in the Wild Card Series. Game 1 in the Bronx, Aaron Boone had to choose his starter. He had former Cy Young winner Gerrit Cole. He had Max Fried, but he chose Schlittler, and Schlittler showed up.

Let's rewind to February. The headline in Tampa wasn't about Schlittler's velocity. It was about his back. Inflammation and a lat issue kept him off the mound for weeks; he fell behind in camp, and with Cole still in rehab from Tommy John and Carlos Rodon on the shelf, the 'Yankees' rotation suddenly looked thin. Then came the games.

On March 27 in San Francisco, 5 1/3 innings, surrendered just one hit, and recorded eight strikeouts. Five days later, hosting Seattle, another 6 1/3 scoreless frames. His back wasn't an issue. Opposing lineups certainly were.

Through 16 starts on the bump, he had built an 8-3 record alongside a 1.71 ERA.

The lowest by a Yankee that deep into the season since Whitey Ford in 1964. On June 19th, he had a career-high 13 strikeouts against the Reds over six scoreless innings at the Stadium. Knicks Guard Josh Heart declared that the Cy Young race was over. In June. He made the All-Star team and was lined up to start in the Midsummer Classic. He passed , choosing to stay on his normal schedule. The Yankees were already thinking about October.

The Final line: 14-6, 1.95 ERA, 239 Strikeouts, 0.92 WHIP in 193 ⅔ innings. Here's why that's more than a great season.

1.95 ERA : Best in the American League, and the lowest by a Yankee since Ron Guidry 's 1.74 in 1978. Only Spud Chandler (1.64 in 1943) and Guidry have done better among qualified Yankees

239 strikeouts : Tied Jack Chesbro (1904) for the fourth most in a single season in franchise history.

21 starts allowing one run or fewer : The most in baseball

6.2 fWAR and a .244 opponent OBP : Both tops in the AL

And then there's the road. Some pitchers rely on the home crowd for help, but Schlittler thrives on "boos". Away from the Bronx, he went 8-2 with a 1.16 ERA in 17 starts, holding hitters to a .153 average. Simply great. Those numbers were the best of any pitcher in baseball. This earned him the 2026 Players Choice Awards AL Outstanding Pitcher.

It starts with a four-seamer that lives around 98 mph and comes downhill from a 6-foot-6 frame. This year, he relied on it approximately 44% of the time. Hitters are aware it's on its way. It is of no significance. What distinguishes him as an ace rather than merely a hard thrower is the surrounding elements: three varied fastball types and a curveball that transitioned from a demonstration pitch to a strikeout tool by the conclusion of the season.

Keep in mind, this was not meant to occur. Schlittler was selected in the seventh round from Northeastern in 2022, signed for $205,000, and did not appear on any top-100 prospect list. He started 2025 in Double-A and was promoted in July only because of Clarke Schmidt 's injury. A year and a half later, he's the top pitcher in the American League.

The last fanbase you want to ask about Schlittler is the Boston Red Sox. Last October, after Red Sox fans came after him and his family online, he answered with eight scoreless innings, 12 strikeouts and zero walks in an elimination game.

This year? Same movie, different date. In Game 1 of the Wild Card Series, he struck out the side in the first and went 6 1/3 scoreless with 10 strikeouts, two hits and one walk on a career-high 117 pitches. He threw 32 curveballs, and Boston couldn't touch them whatsoever. The game ended with the Yankees 9, Boston 0. It made him the first-ever Yankee with two scoreless, double-digit strikeout playoff starts.

His Career ERA against Boston, postseason included, was 0.47.

Schlittler said , "If you want to be a legend, which is obviously the goal, you have to do it in the postseason."

This is the part that stings. The Yankees ran into the 98-64 Tampa Bay Rays. With the team down 1-0 in the ALDS, Schlittler took the ball in Game 2 at Tropicana Field and lasted just 4 1/3 innings, charged with four runs as the defense behind him committed four errors. The game ended with the Rays winning 5-2. Tampa finished the sweep two days later. Schlittler didn't blame anyone but himself.

Cole will have something to say about that in 2027. He's still Gerrit Cole. But aces aren't defined by contracts or résumés. They're defined by who gets the ball when the season is on the line. In 2026, that was Schlittler, and it wasn't close.

On Wednesday, he won the Cy Young Award, and he already has the Players' Choice Award for AL Outstanding Pitcher . Now the question isn't whether Cam Schlittler is the guy; it's how long he can keep these performances up.

articles.title: Jayson Tatum is Celtics ‘Name to Know’ Player of the Game in win over Mavericks
articles.summary: Jayson Tatum scored 32 points in just 30 minutes in Sunday's blowout win over the Mavericks.
articles.body:
The Celtics are the hottest team in the Eastern Conference and they put together yet another historic night on Sunday thanks to their star.

Jayson Tatum finished with a game-high 32 points despite not playing the entire fourth quarter in a 131-94 blowout win over the Mavericks. The stellar night makes Tatum Sunday's 'Name to Know.' The Name to Know Player of the Game is sponsored by John's Sewer and Drain Cleaning, the Name to Know when your drains don't flow .

Tatum was red-hot from the field while leading seven different Celtics in double figures during the win. He shot 11-of-18 from the field and 5-of-8 from 3-point range while also posting six rebounds and six assists in his 30 minutes. It was the best shooting night of the season for Tatum from the field and 3-point range, helping Boston put the game away by the midway point of the third quarter. No Celtics starter played in the fourth quarter as Boston's lead never dipped below 29 points in the second half.

Tatum now has posted six or more assists in 11 of his first 12 games as his offensive evolution has continued while taking on even more of a leading role within Boston's offense following the offseason trade of Jaylen Brown.

The All-Star also only played 30 minutes in the win, setting the stage for Boston's entire roster to get ample rest heading into a back-to-back against the Orlando Magic on Monday night.

articles.summary: Magic: The Gathering Star Trek is just a couple weeks old at this point, but lead designer Mark Rosewater has confirmed that there are no plans for additional Star Trek sets.
articles.body:
Magic: The Gathering Star Trek is just a couple weeks old at this point, but head designer Mark Rosewater has confirmed that there are no plans for additional Star Trek sets.

Star Trek was the latest MTG Universes Beyond set, which boasts 497 cards from across all of the franchise's history. It's a similar approach to how Wizards of the Coast handled Marvel Superheroes earlier this year, which also covered a wide swatch of the comics franchise. But, while Marvel has a set right around the corner in April 2027 with Darkhold Destiny, WotC will not be returning to the final frontier.

Rosewater replied to a question on his Tumblr, speculating on where future Star Trek Magic sets may go, saying flat-out that "there are no current plans for future Star Trek sets." The 'question' Rosewater was responding to came from user yodasws and called out Darkhold Destiny specifically, and speculated that the next Star Trek set could cover something like the Dominion War, which would focus on a huge portion of Deep Space 9. Or, even more specifically, a set based in the Delta Quadrant.

Magic the Gathering: Star Trek – IGN Exclusive Card Reveals

In the same post, Rosewater also denied that Marvel Superheroes was a generic Marvel set, saying, "Marvel Super Heroes wasn’t generic. It was what we called 'Avengers plus,' it was a specific slice of the property."

Rather than focusing on one big pre-existing Marvel story arc, Darkhold Destiny is Wizards of the Coast taking Marvel's IP and creating their own story out of it. WotC worked alongside Marvel to create something entirely new, rather than paying homage to a pre-existing storyline like yodasws speculated.

When Darkhold Destiny comes out next year, it’ll be the third Marvel set to come to Magic: The Gathering, and there are likely going to be many more over the next few years. After all, Marvel’s Spider-Man and Marvel Superheroes each had their own Infinity Stone, the Soul Stone, and Mind Stone, respectively... and there are still six more to go.

But while there won’t be any more Star Trek sets coming to Magic, there are plenty of valuable cards to collect, and it turns out that even Brandon Sanderson is a huge fan .
